english.title: Sell raw cows' milk for direct human consumption in contravention of para 4 of Sch 6 - distributor
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),being a distributor, sold raw cows' milk intended for direct human consumption other than that bought pursuant to paragraph 3(b)(iii) of Schedule 6 to the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006 in the containers in which you had received the milk, with the fasteners of the containers unbroken, from a vehicle which was lawfully used as a shop premises, direct to the final consumer, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF SALE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 17(2) of and paragraph 2(3) of Schedule 6 to the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006.

english.notes: A distributor may only sell raw cows' milk intended for direct human consumption which he or she has bought pursuant to sub-paragraph (b)(iii) of paragraph 3 in the containers in which he or she receives the milk, with the fastenings of the containers unbroken from a vehicle which is lawfully used as a shop premises and directly to the final consumer.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two Years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
No prosecution for an offence under these Regulations which is punishable under paragraph (2) of regulation 17 may be begun after the expiry of (a) three years from the commission of the offence; or (b) one year from its discovery by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
